headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write and execute in the workspace while PaddleOCR can process documents/images, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP/browser tools, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can output text that Cline may treat as instructions if chained. The shared filesystem bridge makes injection plausible in default setups, though not inherently automatic.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into a workspace file that Cline reads
IF Cline is configured to act on file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep OCR outputs in a separate folder not watched by Cline
Prefix OCR outputs with a fixed non-instruction header
Require manual review before Cline consumes OCR text
Disable automatic ingestion of newly created files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between OCR and coding agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. Because Cline shares state via filesystem and has broad network egress, sensitive document contents can flow from shared workspace into its outputs or external calls. PaddleOCR’s allowlisted egress reduces but does not eliminate leakage risk.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the shared workspace
IF Cline is allowed to read those files before OCR redaction
mitigations: Store sensitive docs outside the shared workspace
Redact documents before OCR processing
Restrict Cline to a read-only subset of files
Review outbound network destinations for Cline
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; PaddleOCR can call APIs and run browsers. Their overlapping access to shared mutable resources can create conflicts, especially through the filesystem bridge and concurrent workspace edits. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so default coordination is insufficient.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF PaddleOCR writes derived artifacts that Cline also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Have one agent operate read-only
Commit changes from only one agent at a time
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or actions from OCR-derived text, and PaddleOCR can transform documents/images into text that may be treated as authoritative. If Cline consumes PaddleOCR output without verification, errors or hallucinated text can cascade into downstream edits or browser actions. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Cline uses PaddleOCR output as source material for edits or commands
IF no human or automated verification step checks OCR accuracy
mitigations: Require a human spot-check of OCR output
Compare OCR text against the source image for critical fields
Limit Cline to drafting, not executing, OCR-derived actions
Mark OCR output as untrusted in prompts
requires-engineering: add confidence-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. The main concern is that Cline handles browser screenshots and source code while PaddleOCR handles documents/images, which could create policy mismatch only if regulated data is introduced. The other agent is not cited because no residency or certification mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed through the pair
IF an external policy requires residency or certification not declared here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Add a data-classification checklist before processing
Document retention and deletion expectations
Route regulated workloads to approved systems
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations
